articles.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research
articles.selectionReason: Open full-text paper; topic brain_computer_interface; quality signal passed; application scenario is clear.

paperCard.problem: 脑电信号要用于脑机接口、认知评估、睡眠监测，但“为什么这个模型表现不好、该改哪里”往往说不清。固定流程和奖励驱动的自动搜索不会明确判断信号结构、表征、预测器行为、训练动态各自贡献了多少误差，导致干预手段选得没有依据。
paperCard.method: NeuroAct 用“双环自主研究”来解：内环里设协调者（Coordinator）、研究员（Researcher）、开发者（Developer）、评审者（Reviewer）四种角色，围绕一个目标拆成多个并行问题，用文献、数据语义、模型行为和训练证据提出竞争性假设，再通过可执行的实验去验证，依据性能、稳定性、成本反馈决定下一步；外环把结果提炼成“在什么任务、什么模型条件下适用”的可测试建议，在后续任务中检验、修正或收窄适用范围。
paperCard.difference: 和 BrainAgent（编排信号分析工具）、BrainPilot（固定预处理与训练下做架构研究）、NeuroWeaver（搜索领域受限的流水线）相比，NeuroAct 强调先做“诊断”再选干预，并且明确支持 EEG 基础模型适配、多任务联合训练、模型组合（看模型间错误是否重叠）这些更广的动作空间，还把跨任务经验的条件化复用写进了机制里。
paperCard.innovation: 三点：一是证据引导的内环研究——用信号、表征、预测器、训练四类证据来挑选分析与干预；二是外环的条件化策略改进——经验被写成带适用条件、支持证据、反证据和重估条件的建议，被新任务检验后保留、修正或废弃；三是把 EEG 通用分析、跨任务模型优化、单任务开放研究、协同预测四类场景都做成了可执行的评测设置。另外还有渐进式能力披露（先给能力索引，按需展开细节）来控制上下文。
paperCard.implementation: 协调者按公式选择研究决策与角色派单，每个交接单都记录要交付什么、有哪些证据、还有什么未决问题；研究员用文献与数据证据提方案，开发者写代码跑分析或训练（可并行跑多个 GPU 实验），评审者挑战站不住的结论并回传协调者整合。角色策略靠提示词驱动而非训练，所以行为能随积累的证据变化而不需要改模型参数；经验条目在后续任务中先匹配摘要再取细节，超出预算或被反证就收窄、暂停或替换。
paperCard.applications: 脑机接口解码、认知负荷与认知状态评估（Workload）、睡眠监测（HMC）、年龄预测（HBN）、运动想象（PhysioMI、BCIC-IV-2a）、ADFTD 等神经疾病相关分析，以及作为 EEG 基础模型（如 EEGPT）的自动适配与多模型协同预测工具。
technicalTerms: EEG：脑电图，从头皮电极记录的大脑电活动信号

zh.title: NeuroAct：用双环自主研究智能体推进脑电分析与解码
zh.highlight: 经验复用把 BCIC-IV-2a 的平衡准确率从 34.66% 提升到 50.81%，同时把 LLM token 消耗降低 64.02%。

zh.failureAnalysis: 目前只是 arXiv 预印本（2026 年 10 月），尚未经过同行评审；评测只覆盖 6 个数据集和 3 个 LLM 后端，外部基线也只有 CodeAct、BrainPilot、BrainAgent，成绩高度依赖所选大模型（如 DeepSeek-V4 Flash）与预算设定。

paperCard.problem: 脑电信号要用于脑机接口、认知评估、睡眠监测，但“为什么这个模型表现不好、该改哪里”往往说不清。固定流程和奖励驱动的自动搜索不会明确判断信号结构、表征、预测器行为、训练动态各自贡献了多少误差，导致干预手段选得没有依据。
paperCard.method: NeuroAct 用“双环自主研究”来解：内环里设协调者（Coordinator）、研究员（Researcher）、开发者（Developer）、评审者（Reviewer）四种角色，围绕一个目标拆成多个并行问题，用文献、数据语义、模型行为和训练证据提出竞争性假设，再通过可执行的实验去验证，依据性能、稳定性、成本反馈决定下一步；外环把结果提炼成“在什么任务、什么模型条件下适用”的可测试建议，在后续任务中检验、修正或收窄适用范围。
paperCard.difference: 和 BrainAgent（编排信号分析工具）、BrainPilot（固定预处理与训练下做架构研究）、NeuroWeaver（搜索领域受限的流水线）相比，NeuroAct 强调先做“诊断”再选干预，并且明确支持 EEG 基础模型适配、多任务联合训练、模型组合（看模型间错误是否重叠）这些更广的动作空间，还把跨任务经验的条件化复用写进了机制里。
paperCard.innovation: 三点：一是证据引导的内环研究——用信号、表征、预测器、训练四类证据来挑选分析与干预；二是外环的条件化策略改进——经验被写成带适用条件、支持证据、反证据和重估条件的建议，被新任务检验后保留、修正或废弃；三是把 EEG 通用分析、跨任务模型优化、单任务开放研究、协同预测四类场景都做成了可执行的评测设置。另外还有渐进式能力披露（先给能力索引，按需展开细节）来控制上下文。
paperCard.implementation: 协调者按公式选择研究决策与角色派单，每个交接单都记录要交付什么、有哪些证据、还有什么未决问题；研究员用文献与数据证据提方案，开发者写代码跑分析或训练（可并行跑多个 GPU 实验），评审者挑战站不住的结论并回传协调者整合。角色策略靠提示词驱动而非训练，所以行为能随积累的证据变化而不需要改模型参数；经验条目在后续任务中先匹配摘要再取细节，超出预算或被反证就收窄、暂停或替换。
paperCard.applications: 脑机接口解码、认知负荷与认知状态评估（Workload）、睡眠监测（HMC）、年龄预测（HBN）、运动想象（PhysioMI、BCIC-IV-2a）、ADFTD 等神经疾病相关分析，以及作为 EEG 基础模型（如 EEGPT）的自动适配与多模型协同预测工具。

en.highlight: Experience reuse raised BCIC-IV-2a balanced accuracy from 34.66% to 50.81% while cutting LLM token usage by 64.02%.
en.summary: This preprint introduces NeuroAct, an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis and decoding: an inner loop in which Researcher, Developer, and Reviewer roles test competing diagnostic hypotheses through executable experiments, and an outer loop that distills results into conditional recommendations validated and revised across tasks. Evaluated on six datasets, three LLM backends, and four research settings, it reports large gains, such as an 80.88 macro-average versus BrainAgent's 63.13 and a 16.33-point balanced-accuracy improvement on ADFTD. It is worth reading because it makes the diagnostic decision itself — which analysis or intervention to try — the object of automation, rather than relying on fixed pipelines or reward-driven search.
en.failureAnalysis: It is only an arXiv preprint (October 2026) without peer review, and the evaluation covers just six datasets, three LLM backends, and three external baselines, so results depend heavily on the chosen backend and budget settings.
en.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research

paperCard.problem: EEG analysis and decoding underlie brain-computer interfaces, cognitive assessment, and sleep monitoring, but fixed pipelines and reward-driven search do not explicitly determine how signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics contribute to performance or generalization gaps, leaving intervention choice underdetermined.
paperCard.method: NeuroAct runs a dual-loop autonomous research process: an inner loop where a Coordinator directs Researcher, Developer, and Reviewer roles across parallel questions, testing competing hypotheses with executable analyses and choosing next actions from performance, stability, and cost feedback; and an outer loop that distills outcomes into conditional, testable recommendations and validates or revises them on later tasks.
paperCard.difference: Unlike BrainAgent (tool orchestration), BrainPilot (architecture research under fixed preprocessing and training), and NeuroWeaver (domain-constrained pipeline search), NeuroAct diagnoses gaps from signal, representation, predictor, and training evidence before choosing interventions, and it explicitly covers EEG foundation-model adaptation, joint multi-task training, and model combination via cross-model error overlap.
paperCard.innovation: Three parts: evidence-guided inner-loop research that uses signal, representation, predictor, and training evidence to select analyses or interventions; outer-loop conditional strategy improvement, where experience is stored with applicable task and model conditions, supporting and counterevidence, and reassessment conditions; and executable operationalization across four settings — EEG General Analysis, Cross-task Model Optimization, Single-task Open Research, and Collaborative Prediction.
paperCard.implementation: The Coordinator selects a research decision and specialist assignments, dispatching Researcher, Developer, and Reviewer in separate contexts; each handoff records the requested deliverable, supporting evidence, unresolved issues, and a recommendation. Roles are prompted rather than trained, so behavior evolves with accumulated evidence without LLM parameter updates. Experiments run in parallel when GPU resources permit, and experience entries are matched by summary before details are disclosed on demand.
paperCard.applications: Brain-computer interface decoding, cognitive workload and state assessment, sleep monitoring, age prediction, motor imagery, ADFTD and other clinical EEG analyses, plus automated adaptation of EEG foundation models such as EEGPT and multi-model collaborative prediction.
technicalTerms: EEG: electrical brain activity recorded from scalp electrodes
EEG-FM: a foundation model pretrained on large EEG corpora and adaptable to downstream tasks
Inner/outer loop: the inner loop runs hypothesis-experiment-review cycles within a task; the outer loop distills, validates, and revises experience across tasks
Balanced accuracy (BA): the average of per-class accuracies, robust to class imbalance
Pearson's r: a correlation coefficient measuring linear agreement between predictions and targets
BrainBench: the benchmark used for general EEG analysis evaluation
Progressive disclosure: giving agents a compact capability index first and expanding details on demand to conserve context
Conditional experience: recommendations written with applicability conditions, used when matched and revised by outcomes
CodeAct / BrainAgent / BrainPilot: the three external agent baselines compared in the paper

articles.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + HN discussion
articles.summary: OpenShell 是 NVIDIA GitHub 组织下的运行时项目，从标题看，它面向成批自主 AI 智能体，强调安全与隐私。该条目在 Hacker News 获得 501 分和 217 条评论，说明多智能体安全执行是受关注议题；值得读的点在于它如何落地部署，以及会受哪些工程与合规约束。
articles.failureAnalysis: 安全私密运行时若不能兼容主流智能体框架和工具链，企业迁移成本会很高；成批运行还要求隔离、资源调度、可观测性和故障恢复等工程能力。合规审计、责任边界和数据治理也会抬高采用门槛。仅有 HN 高热度不足以证明真实采购需求或长期维护投入，项目可能停留在演示阶段。

en.summary: OpenShell is a GitHub project under NVIDIA that positions itself as a safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Its Hacker News discussion—501 points and 217 comments—signals strong interest in secure multi-agent execution, making its deployment path and constraints worth examining.
en.failureAnalysis: The project may struggle if it cannot integrate with existing agent frameworks, keep isolation and observability manageable at fleet scale, or satisfy enterprise compliance and audit requirements. Strong HN attention alone does not prove sustained adoption or a clear buyer.
